description: This program invites participants to critically examine how policy shapes access, equity, and influence—and how it can be reshaped to respectfully enact diverse worldviews and lived experiences. description: Period of Residency: From January to December 2027 Possible duration from 1 to 6 months. Recommended minimum duration 2 months. Shared (2-3 artists) and private studios are available, along with weekly artist lunch gatherings and connections to a local network of artists and traditional artisans. Enjoy a balance of focused production and research along with creative community and cultural immersion to stir your work to new levels. Applications for our 3 or 6 week artist-funded residency seasons are being taken on an open basis for the available 8 studio spaces each season. Completed and approved applications (including a video interview) will be assessed by our local selection panel before a final decision is made. Travel, housing, meals, and supplies are not included in the residency fee.

title: Residency 500 € / month from October to December 2018 in Finland!
description: Haihatus is a place to focus on making art and getting inspired. Haihatus artist residency aims to collaboration and communication between arts and artists. There is a lot of space to make art and colleagues to work and spend time with. Own space and time is also available and respected. The former residency artists have valued it's relaxed and free atmosphere. You can also arrange your own happenings to perform your own art. Or you can just rest and get inspired by the forests and lakes in Finland and find new international artist friends. Haihatus is an easygoing place to be. Haihatus is located in a rural community called Joutsa. The distance from Helsinki to Joutsa is 200 km and from the nearest city Jyväskylä 70 km. Nature in Joutsa is beautiful and the seasonal change is very affective. There are forests to ramble and lakes to swim - or ski and ice skate in winter. There is also a free of charge Gym near Haihatus.

title: Canadian Summer Artist Residency (1 week to 2 months)
costs: CA$15.00 application fee CA$363.00 program fee
description: Spark Box Studio’s Artist Residency Program provides live/work space to accommodate both emerging and professional printmakers, photographers, painters, illustrators and writers. Artists-in-residence have access to our professional studio and resources. The Residency Program affords artists the space and time to support the advancement of their careers and to strengthen their practice. Our program also offers a variety of career building opportunities for artists including our Emerging Artist Guide, opportunities for business workshops with local professionals and consultations with local artists and curators. Artists-in-residence stay with us, Chrissy and Kyle, in a charming century home located just outside the town of Picton in Prince Edward County, Ontario, Canada. Interested artists may apply to live and work at Spark Box for a duration of one weekend to 2 months.

title: Open Call 2018-2019
description: Art Print Residence offers its professional printmaking workshop to visual artists who desire to develope their own project. Art Print Residence is specialized in intaglio printmaking and woodcut, so Master platemaker can give technical advice and personal assistance to the artists (if the artists need it). APR can also accomodate artists of other disciplines like writers, drawers, illustrators... Residency period: minimum 1 week – maximum 3 months In case the artist needs a longer period to develop his project we can study this possibility. The artists in residence must live in the apartment during the residency. Our shop is divided into several specific work areas. Mechanical zone with a wide variety of saws, milling machines, guillotines, flexible shafts, drills, and a set of electrical tools. Artists are able to work on metal materials (copper) as well as on plastic and wood. We can accommodate copper plates up to a maximum size of 100×200 cm. 39.3×78.74 inches.

title: How to write about Contemporary Art at the Royal College of Art
description: How to Write About Contemporary Art is a week-long short course at the Royal College of Art delivered by esteemed Head of Writing and author Dr Brian Dillon. Join the RCA in London this summer to learn about writing, pitching and making it as an arts writer from 30 July–3 August. Taught and delivered by Dr Brian Dillon is the Acting Head of MA Writing at the RCA plus guest speakers and visiting lecturers. Dillon has written many books on art and culture, including Essayism (2017), Objects in This Mirror (2014) and In the Dark Room (2005). He writes about contemporary art for frieze, Artforum, the Guardian and London Review of Books. He has curated exhibitions for Tate and the Hayward Gallery, and is an editor of Cabinet, an art and culture magazine based in New York. Dynamic dialogue on a range of topics featuring keynote lectures from widely published critics, close reading of criticism in seminars, writing workshops and visits to current exhibitions.

title: Summer and Fall Residencies at the International Center for the Arts
organizationName: The International center for the Arts
description: ICA residencies are open to creative individuals and scholars from across the disciplinary spectrum of the visual and performing arts, literature, and all areas of the humanities. They are available on a weekly basis, ranging from as little as one week to as long as three months. Our residencies are family-friendly and ICA provides many options for accommodation of spouses or partners, family members and children, with a range of activities for those guests not participating in the Residency program. ICA Residencies are all-inclusive and provide: airport transfer from the Rome (Fiumicino) Airport, airport welcome and departure service, double or single accommodation (private apartments are available for an additional fee), three chef-catered meals per day, private studio space, one excursion per week to cities such as Rome and Florence, and ongoing bilingual support 24/7. Facilities for drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, ceramics, and photography are available.

title: Artistic Lodging + Shared Studio | Tomaz Hipólito Studio | OPEN CALL
description: AZAN residency program aims to welcome artists and introduce them to the Lisbon art scene with the feeling of a shared studio where artists can collaborate, share ideas and develop their work and research. Dialogue and experimentation are encouraged and projects related to the studio and its surroundings are welcomed. Our team will work with each resident in a supportive environment providing curatorial and production support. We can provide information about openings, art events and suppliers, maximizing the exposure of each resident in the city. Residents are encouraged to organize a talk, a work presentation, a happening, a pop-up exhibition during their stay and participate in the zines project. All the events are organized between the artist and AZAN team, in a case-by-case basis. General . Private bedroom + shared studio, kitchen and bathroom Conditions Water, electricity and wi-fi included in the fee . Option I: Room + 70 m2 studio . Option II: Room + 100 m2 studio

title: Ceramic Residency in India
description: The Ceramic residency is open to practising artists who can work on their own project or take a break. The residency does not expect the artist to have any output except that they make optimum use of the time and resources to do what they wish to. Participation with local community and students, presentations or open studios are welcome. The city of Baroda has over 1000 artists living and working here. the school of fine arts and performing arts make this place ideal for any artist to spend fruitful time in the city. There are many community studios and art galleries too It is a fully furnished clay studio. For more details please see our URL www.nehalrachh.com or write to neh2310@gmail.com

title: International Sculpture Day
description: International Sculpture Day, ISC’s most anticipated event of the year returns on Saturday, April 30th! Join the global sculpture community when you register your event and use #ISDAY on Twitter, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube. Suggested types of in person and virtual events include demonstrations, exhibitions, iron pours, open studios, panels, workshops and more!

title: Unique artist residency opportunity
description: The residency programs are established to support both artists and nature lovers by offering them a chance to have a peaceful place to create and grow within nature. The Residency Programs allows each visitor to experience their place, the surroundings and find their muse in the silence of the night. We believe that nature is a great inspiration for artistic expression and learning. We can confirm ... it really is! Being for a while at the place where the clouds are born provides new inspiration for life.

title: Khai-Káng AIR Open Call
description: Debuted at the 2019 Taiwan Lantern Festival in Pingtung, Khai-Káng is a new multi-purpose creative hub situated in a Japanese-style heritage house located in a cultural & creative village in Pingtung. The objective of Khai-Káng is to bring people together and provide a fun and unique platform for artistic & cultural exchange. Khai-Káng provides accommodation and studio space free of charge (for a limited time only). Artists are responsible for all other costs including personal living expenses, transport/travel costs, art supplies, and insurance. Duration of residency is flexible (for at least one month). Artists receive professional support and networking opportunities. Resident artists are expected to present their work in a format of their choice, such as an artist talk and/or exhibition. In addition, artists are required to leave work(s) behind for the permanent collection of Khai-Káng.

title: OPEN CALL Residency "Creative Ecologies and Decolonial Futurities"
location: San Cristóbal de las Casas, Mexico
description: The next residency at Casa Giap will take place in San Cristobal de Las Casas from July 22 to 31 and it will be coordinated by GIAP (Research group in art and politics) and TJ Demos (University of California – Santa Cruz). The program includes seminars with GIAP (Research Group in Art and Politics), Professor TJ Demos, and local guests. It will involve some field trips (one towards the interior of the forest, at a site of environmental/social interest) and many other activities, such as meetings with Mayan artists. You can consult the report that TJ Demos wrote about last summer’s residency: https://rca.ucsc.edu/documents/open-forum-fall-2018-tj-demos-final.pdf The participation cost for each resident is $ 700 USD. It covers: – Program of seminars, talks and meetings – 11 nights accommodation (with kitchen and wifi) – Access to media library and GIAP’s art collection – Transfers outside the city – Some food and coffee break between sessions.

title: Nes, a remote artist residency in the stunning location of northwest Iceland
description: The aim of the program is to provide artists with the space and time to focus on their art practice with few distractions. The residency is loosely structured with 3 events each month: free format artists presentations, a public open studio event, and a shared potluck dinner. In order to keep our residency fees low and artistic freedom high, the Nes team provides accessory site support: we are on the sideline to assist with any logistical issues or artistic questions that arise as needed . We view our role in the residency more as supporters rather than managers or administrators.

title: Residency at "Palazzo del Gatto" - Summer 2019
description: Artists are hosted at “Palazzo del Gatto”, in the medieval village of Casaprota, (Sabine region, in the centre of Italy). They have access to studio and working spaces, located inside the Palazzo and in the large garden with a fantastic inspirational landscape. Inside the Palazzo, there are four bedrooms, single and double, and three ½ bathrooms, a kitchen, a dining room, two living rooms, the original storeroom (now a multifunctional space and study hall), and a wine cavern. The nearby municipal theatre is available for performers, as well as the adjacent exhibition hall. During their residency, artists are asked to develop a project that establishes a relationship with the territory and/or its inhabitants. Artists have opportunities to interact with locals and to visit the surroundings. At the end of the residency works are exhibited to the community.

title: LUX ARTIST RESIDENCY IN KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia
organizationName: LA FENICE ART GALLERY - HONG KONG
description: LUX ARTIST RESIDENCY IN KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia It is ideal for artists who want to create in luxury in the tropical climate of Southeast Asia. La Fenice Art Gallery makes this apartment available to selected promising artists for a few months every year. An apartment with 3 bedrooms, two bathrooms on 22 floor of a resort style condo with luxury swimming pool and stunning views of the city and a mountain covered by lush jungle and populated by monkeys and beautiful tropical birds. Located in Northern part of Kuala Lumpur, 15 minutes walk away from famous Batu Caves Temple. KTM public train service to the city is 15 min walk away. The rental price includes utility bills. Local prepaid sim card with calls and internet will cost you about 50 cents per day. There is a coin laundry in the building, plus cafes, 2 supermarkets... This studio is ideal for those of you who want to explore this booming part of the world and living a luxury lifestyle...

title: APPLICATION OPEN: 360 minute Creative Residency throughout NYC
description: Holes in the Wall Collective invites you to spend 360 minutes in an unlikely residency space somewhere in the five boroughs of NYC. An office, a workshop, a grocery isle, the recycling plant... to leave your routine for One Day. Six hours. 360 minutes. To work creatively on a project. Something you are writing, researching, creating, observing. At any part of your process. How it works: You apply. If accepted, we match you (and your work) to a residency space somewhere in NYC. We confirm the date. We give you 6 hours, coffee and an introduction with your space. Sometime during your residency, you give us one blog post that says something about your 360 minutes. An image, a haiku, a paragraph, an animation. We then host a public event at the end of the year to bring together all the residents & their work. It’s free to apply and to participate. Residencies held on select Saturdays & Wednesdays starting in May. apply at https://www.holesinthewallcollective.org/360-residency

title: OCAD University: CONTEMPORARY FLORENCE STUDIO - Spring and Summer Open Session: Creator in Residence
description: Open Session: Creator in Residence Spring: April 12th - 18th, April 19th-26th, 2019 Duration: 1 week or 2 weeks (participant can select) and Summer: July 8th - 14th, July 15th- 22nd, 2019 Duration: 1 week or 2 weeks (participant can select) Immerse yourself in a city where the rich traditions of fine art and craftsmanship meet contemporary art and design! As a participant, you will receive access to space at OCAD U’s Florence studio in Florence’ San Marco neighbourhood. Your own designated work space will be complemented by the proximity to other creative professionals from around the world, as well as an array of programming to help you reflect on and share your practice. The residency includes an introductory Italian lesson, group community events, studio visits with local practitioners.

title: Artist in Residence
description: The Access Arts residency program is relatively new (launched in 2014), though the organization has been around since 1971. At any given time, there could be up to 8 AIR in various media. Resident artists conduct classes and perform studio maintenance and community outreach tasks. In return, they are provided with studio space, use of equipment, some materials, and group and/or solo exhibition opportunities. Mainly we are seeking clay, fiber, and documentary film artists currently, but will accept applications for other media/projects.

title: BELGRADE ART STUDIO Residency 2018/2019
description: Residency in a private air-conditioned fully furnished apartment which is unique and has character, in Dorcol historic building, built in 1921-23. Living in Dorćol has its charms, it could be like living in Kreuzberg in Berlin or Manhattan in NYC. A sense of history, with the pieces of furniture from 1920s and original wooden floor, windows, doors and a fully functional kitchen for the self-catering of residents, bathroom, dining/sitting room, studio. A painting studio is equipped with easels, stool, ample wall space, both natural and artificial lighting and a small library.The space was renovated over the course of a whole year and decorated following an ‘‘eclectic luxury’’ approach that combines vintage design with contemporary art. Complimentary pick-up and drop-off for arrival and departure, welcoming traditional serbian meal, private Belgrade City tour, a studio representative always on hand to help out and lots more, check out http://belgradeartstudio.com/studio-accommodation/

title: Summer in Istanbul at halka art project
description: halka art project invites visual artists, writers, musicians, performers, story tellers, curators, poets, cultural researchers among others to apply to its residency programme. The weekly residency fee for a single artist is €375 and €550 for artist dous or couples who want to share a private room. On the other hand, halka art project is happy to announce that it is not an artist hotel. We expect to see the end result of each residency periods. For stays longer than a month we organize exhibitions for the local audience and art circles. For shorter visits we encourage our artists to hold an artist talk to share their experience so that the residency term would not be an exotic trip to Istanbul. Our team of curators, art managers and artist assistants help our residents in every step of the realization of their projects on day to day basis. We use our network for the promotion of the residency projects and for our guests to meet with the local audience and professionals.

title: Gilsfjordur, Iceland - a remote residency from April to October
description: The attraction of this residency is the distance and quiet and beautiful location at the end a long fjord. The old farmhouse is very remote, a dirt and rock track 12km from the nearest village of Kroksfjardarnes. Artists will live together alone in the house. The sounds will be the wind, distant waterfalls, perhaps some sheep and birds. An ideal spot for planning, drawing, photography, video, thinking, writing, walking. There will be opportunities to connect with local community and your folklorist and farm (off site) resident manager has a long family history with the land and will provide information about the surrounding areas of the Westfjords.

title: Sointula Art Shed 2020 Residencies Available
description: Currently accepting applications for the months of October, November, and December still available in 2019. We will post at a later date when we are accepting for 2020.

title: Artist Residency in Tufo
description: Rosa di Tufo is the ancestral home of the DeVito family, recently converted into a Bed and Breakfast. We offer reduced rates for artists in the form of a residency--$150 per week, or $550 per month. This residency is truly remote--not only is Tufo seated in a rural area of Southern Italy, the house itself is internet-free. (There is a 24-hour cafe down the street that offers wifi for free and espressos for eighty cents.) As Tufo is a small town (pop. ~1,000), its residents won't miss you. They are generally welcoming to artists, and will often engage with you in town and, sometimes, invite you to enormous, late dinners. Inquiries to program director Patrick DeVito McNeil at rosaditufo@gmail.com.

title: PERMANENT CALL - Art and research residency in San Cristóbal de Las Casas, Chiapas
location: San Cristóbal de las Casas, Mexico
description: The contents of the program are adjusted to the needs and interests of each individual or group of participants. We offer a series of seminars, meetings, experiences, excursions, and moments of creation and collective work facilitated by GIAP (Research Group in Art and Politics, founded in 2013 by Natalia Arcos and Alessandro Zagato) and other local invitees (artists, gallerists, researchers, and activists.) Our aim is to explore forms of resistant art, in a context like Chiapas, where Mayan and revolutionary traditions inspire us daily. The fee includes: 15 nights of accommodation 13 Working days Transfers to field sites Access to GIAP’s media library and art collection Working areas and facilities Some meals

title: Collective Studio Residency
description: The residency program at Con Artist Collective offers 24/7 studio access to artists for just $400/month. The best thing about our community are the amazing artists who have affiliated themselves with us in one way or another. We ask our members that are enjoying success, or doing interesting and innovative work to jury our regular pool of applicants for exceptional talent. More than a studio, the shared workspace at Con Artist Collective holds regular events like: - Life Drawing - Critique Club (get feedback on your work!) - Art Business Talks (get answers to your questions about the art world!) - Practical Workshops (on topics like optimizing your social media, photoshop, screen printing, 3D-printing, framing, artistic technique and more!) *EXCLUSIVE TO STUDIO RESIDENTS:* - A monthly showcase of work made here in the studio - Featured on Artsy.net

title: ‘Residency on the Ocean’ - Call for Participants, Sail Britain
description: Sail Britain is an interdisciplinary project working towards positive change for the oceans through sailing, creative practice and the development and exchange of ideas. Examining our relationship with the sea while learning how to sail an ocean-going vessel allows privileged insights into an inaccessible environment. The programme will work with crew members from the arts, sciences and communities to explore issues such as marine plastic pollution, Climate Change, singing on the sea, the cultural importance of islands, and what it means to be small on a big Blue Planet!

title: Immersive Listening Retreat in Italy
description: Piano Piano Immersive Listening Retreat, 21-26th June 2019, Basilicata, South of Italy Immerse yourself in the pristine soundscape of Italy’s largest national park, and open your ears. Gently guided by a professional sound artist, 6 participants will stay in a beautifully restored Palazzo from 1822 (with daily breakfast and full use of kitchen, meditation spaces and panoramic terrace) and enjoy daily site-specific soundwalks, ear cleansing exercises, listening sessions and outdoor activities designed to reconnect with the power of listening in all its forms: as an opening to the natural soundscape, to each other, and to our own inner voice. Excursions include one full day in Matera - 2019 European City of Culture. Breakfast, 24/hr use of kitchen and wi-fi are also included. For full details and what is included, please visit the link.

title: Your Art Residency in Argentina!
description: The Residencia Corazón – Artist in Residency -A-i-R- Program was initiated in 2006. Its main objective engenders the creation of a personalized and independent exchange among regional, national and international artists. It allows for mutual enrichment through professional and emotive approaches for new experiences and aesthetic realities. The resident / visiting artists enjoy a dynamic and vibrant time frame for working; they have a studio and living space at their disposal to complete their projects. They also network with and within the local art community, cultural institutions and the public at large. Residencia Corazón offers a complete international Artist in Residency Program. Each artist, curator or writer receives exclusive and highly-personalised support from the Residencia Corazón team. Our goal is to give the resident an experience that transcends the artistic and that he/she will treasure throughout his/her life.

title: The Akaliko Residency | Amalgam
description: The artists at the residency will be exploring ideas from their own creative practices with others over the micro residency period and help develop some context in the process to produce ‘any collaborative output’ in an organic way. Hence the name for this edition is “Amalgam”, as we look forward to see elements new and old practiced by a small pool of diverse groups of people creating the much-needed synergy. The residency will accommodate 8 participants alongside 3 host participants and divide them equally into groups at a riverside Savar location, just at the outskirts of Dhaka. The participants can be practicing any form of art/discipline and at all stages. So don’t hold back to register your interest. Register here. The application fee is for confirmed participants only and is refundable.

description: UP and The Museum of Human Achievement foster a welcoming and intentional community of artists and arts administrators, as well as a number of useful tools and facilities at our resident artists' disposal. Our building is equipped with a dark room, co-working space, 1000 sq ft gallery space, venue area with PA, vinyl record cutting lathe, VR headset, tool library and various audio/visual equipment. Both the gallery and the venue host monthly exhibitions, weekly performance events and occasional educational programming; artists in residence are encouraged to participate in the development of our programming activities. MoHA is located in a thriving neighborhood near multiple local restaurants, work-focused coffee shops and businesses, as well as a multitude of neighboring art/creative spaces, including Canopy, Big Medium, Tillery Park, and Bolm Studios. Hybrid space between creation factory an art gallery, Piramidón merges the field of artistic production with the field of dissemination, exhibition and sale of works of art. The Facilities during the residency: Possibility of exhibit the work in the gallery space, Information of the artist (exhibitions, works, talks…) on social networks (Facebook, Instagram, Twitter), on the website and in “Piramidón News” (Biannual newsletter of the various exhibitions and activities of the artists of Piramidón) Free access to the kitchen-office, free use of the dining room/or meeting room, water and electricity service, free access to the rooftop terrace, free use of the tools and machinery, free wifi access, printing facilities, storage and temporary custody of artist personal belongings.

title: SHORT-TERM PRINTMAKING ARTIST IN RESIDENCE

description: The purpose of the Artist in Residence Program is to offer artists the opportunity to use the studio space at Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design. The Centre offers residencies to artists in one or more of the following media: ceramics, metal and jewellery, stained glass, printmaking and textiles. Artists in residence are given access to these studios at a subsidized studio rental rate. Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design offers residencies of flexible lengths from two weeks to six months.

title: Open Call
description: Phoenix Athens aims to create a fully developed residency programme which will support and promote artists' work. An Athens based curator will work with each artist individually throughout their stay to support their research, practice and onsite public/ community projects. The curator will be in discussion with the artists’ prior and during their stay in Athens in order to provide a rounded collaboration. The residency aims to motivate artists to develop their practice and research inspired by the rich culture of the city. Phoenix Athens proposes to create a dialogue between the current residents and the social, political and cultural history of the city. Artists are welcomed to produce small and large scale of work using all the facilities mentioned below. Artists are welcomed to facilitate a workshop based on their practice or provide a talk/presentation in order to present their work and research to the public.

title: SHORT-TERM METAL & JEWELLERY ARTIST IN RESIDENCE
organizationName: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
description: The purpose of the Artist in Residence program is to offer artists the opportunity to use the studio space at Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design. The Centre offers residencies to artists in one or more of the following media: ceramics, metal and jewellery, stained glass, printmaking and textiles. Artists in residence are given access to these studios at a subsidized studio rental rate. Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design offers residencies of flexible lengths from two weeks to six months.

title: Kooshk Residency Open Call
description: Kooshk offers direct applications for artists applying independently. In the case of direct applications, artists are required to go through the following process: ● Please state briefly why you would like to stay at Kooshk and tell us about your project and what you would like to achieve. Please include the dates you require. Email your proposal to info@kooshkresidency.com ● Once accepted, artists and curators are responsible for securing funding. We are happy to assist artists seeking grants by providing a letter of invitation in their own country. Financial support cannot be provided for the residency but we are happy to support your project with our knowledge, background information and networks. ● There is no deadline and the application review takes place once every month.

title: Artist in Residence at The Factory
description: A 12-week non profit program designed to bring new emerging and amateur artists from around the world to Manchester, NH. Our program fosters an environment that allows creative freedom to explore, define, and polish your working portfolio. Selected applicants are provided a studio apartment with basic household amenities, heat, hot water, electricity & internet provided. Each residency concludes with an artist opening celebration. The Opening acts as a solo or duo exhibition to feature each artist’s developing works. Our onsite event space is set up to feature your installations and presentations to the local community. AIR’s may also organize/host additional public events/programs (artist talks, community dinners, workshop, studio visits, etc.)

title: Open Call for Artists: Introduce Artists to Arrival Gallery and Earn 15% Commission
description: Art moves through people. Arrival Gallery is accepting applications for its Certified Online Agent Programme, a remote opportunity for artists and arts professionals who understand creative communities and can introduce suitable practising artists to international exhibition opportunities. Selected applicants complete the free Arrival Gallery Academy before activation. The academy covers understanding Arrival Gallery, identifying suitable artists, professional outreach, navigating artist forms and submissions, tracking eligible introductions, ethical communication and programme compliance. Once certified, agents use approved links and programme tools to introduce artists to relevant Arrival Gallery opportunities. The role includes starting professional conversations, sharing accurate information, following up respectfully and guiding interested artists to official application or booking pages. Certified agents receive 15% commission on eligible completed bookings attributed to thei

title: Fellini Gallery Open Call
description: Live & Work Studio or Work Studio – Kyoto, Japan FELLINI Gallery Kyoto is an Art Center located a 3-minute walk from an eco-friendly boutique hotel, comprising an international art gallery, ateliers, studios, and residency in the cultural and artistic city of Kyoto, Japan. A long term or short-term residency and exhibition cooperation opportunities with the internationally known gallery are available. Location : We are 3 min walk to the subway stop Sanjo Keihan, along the Kamo river, 5-10 minutes walk to Gion, Pontocho. Cost : Private rooms start from 80000 JPY to 100000 JPY monthly and 10000JPY shared studio monthly. What the residency provides : Monthly rate includes water, electricity, fully furnished Bed linens, towels, a washing machine,maid service, fast free Wi-Fi, kitchen with full utensils. The artist must pay for their own transportation and housing. How to Apply : Please contact by email / residence@fellinigallery.com

title: ACCEPTING APPLICATIONS FOR 2020 WINTER RESIDENCIES
organizationName: Monte Azul Center for the Arts
description: Monte Azul Center for the Arts caters to artists in a number of disciplines & practices. We offer an inclusive residency program where diversity is a creative advantage. Example practices include: Printmaking, Painting, Photography, Writing, Mixed Media, Screen Printing & Group Projects; as well as private studio visits and discussion.

title: Craft 101 2025
description: After the resounding success of Craft 101 in 2024, Arts Letters & Numbers is excited to bring the program back, bigger, more immersive, and more interdisciplinary than ever. Between July 1 and August 30, our Averill Park campus will host over twenty unique programs designed to blend technical skill-building with conceptual exploration. Through hands-on mentorship, material experimentation, and collaborative inquiry, participants will have the freedom to move across disciplines, forging deep connections between ideas, people, and practices. With an expanded lineup of artists, scholars, and practitioners, Craft 101 2025 continues its mission to transform education, pushing boundaries, fostering exchange, and rethinking how we learn and create. Join us in this evolving experiment, where learning isn’t just about acquiring knowledge, it’s about exploration, making, and discovery.

title: ILHABELA ISLAND - BRAZIL 2020 SESSIONS
description: Casa na Ilha is a retreat space to devote time and focus to your creative pursuits in an ecological paradise. Artists can intensely dedicate on their work in progress or develop new projects. The main goal is that artists are able to focus on their ideas and projects, enhancing creativity and inspiration and connect, between them, the local community and nature. We welcome artists with a professional standing in their field and emerging artists of promising talent. The Program is 2 to 4 weeks long duration between 5 - 8 artists at a time. In case projects requires it, participants may apply for a longer period. Applications are accepted from all disciplines. Artists work on a self-directed residency: you will have uninterrupted, self-directed work time. We will not pressure you to deliver finished work; you can focus solely on research and development of ideas.However, during your stay there will be a tutor to discuss ideas, projects and progress of work during their stay.

title: OPEN CALL FOR INTERNATIONAL ARTISTS
description: Three Shadows Photography Art Centre is the first independent organization specializing in contemporary art photography in China. The program aims to provide a platform for international photographers, critics, ​and curators to practice and study photographic art. It also helps create opportunities for artists across the world to have a necessary conversation. Residents are encouraged to design unique projects for themselves during their residency, which could mean working on new commissions, collaborating with other artists, or holding workshops in collaboration with the educational department of Three Shadows. We are ready to provide the facilities, materials, and services that artists need to complete their projects. We’re also willing to introduce them to a diverse group of local artists and support collaborations with local organizations.

title: HONF Foundation Artist in Residency Program
description: Run by HONF Foundation - a laboratory for arts, science and technology, the AiR HONF Artist-in-Residence programme for international artist, technologist, designer, engineer and scientist is based on inter-disciplinary, collaboration and community based project, with the aim of building a dialogue, knowledge sharing, and fostering innovation between foreign artists and practitioners with local communities as well as looking for a creative solutions for today’s urgent needs through arts, science and technology. Resident artist receive a facility to work in HONFablab, the first Fablab in South East Asia with fully equipment, a studio, as well as to present their work at HONF’s Gallery. The artist in residency programme will do an arrangement for the resident artist to present their work publicly through exhibition, performance, projections, public discussions. Please send a cv, portfolio, and short description of your project to honfresidencyprogram@gmail.com for applying this program.

title: L'Expressoir Artist Residency
description: L'Expressoir emphasizes the connection between the local community and the diverse artists this village attracts. This residency encourages projects promoting the interaction and relationships between different cultures worldwide.

title: Artnoise 2020 Open Residency (London, United Kingdom)
description: Artnoise 2020 Open Residency is a year long program designed for Creatives who work in the digital space interested in exploring African arts and take steps in developing their careers and artistic development. This program made of 3-week stays in Lome, London, Accra and Lagos provides time and space for digital creatives such as digital illustrators and painters, video game artists, Youtube content creators and other digital arts professionals to create, research, experiment, cultivate new directions in their work as well as execute new projects. In addition to a shared studio space and living facilities, artists are invited to immerse themselves in the local creative community, art exhibitions and festivals, visit galleries and have the opportunity to learn from their peers in the hosting city. The 3-Week stay in London, UK starts 1st of June 2020 and ends on 21st June 2020,

title: Artnoise 2020 Digital Residency (online)
description: Artnoise offers its first e-Residency, a digital online program that provides participating creatives support and promotion with the opportunity to exhibit in Togo, United Kingdom, Accra and Lagos from any part of the world. Allowing them to reach a wider audience and sell their art. Artnoise 2020 Digital Residency offers the opportunity for Creatives to gain more experience, support, network with other creatives and reach a wider audience. Using the platform to show their working process and give insight into their art. Knowledgeable staff are available to provide technical support and assistance.*

description: Artnoise 2020 Open Residency is a year long program designed for Creatives who work in the digital space interested in exploring African arts and take steps in developing their careers and artistic development. The 3-Week stay in Accra, Ghana starts on the 17th August 2020 and ends 6th of September 2020

The 3-Week stay in Lome, Togo starts on the 16th of March 2020 and ends on the 11th of April 2020

title: CROSSING, SPACE FOR TRANSFORMATION
description: Faced with the new situation brought by COVID-19, we have decided to start a new initiative. Crossing – Space for transformation is intended for those who need a space to create, hold exhibitions or workshops, focus on analysis and/or promotion of their work, for those who wish to have a coworking office or the ones who want to take a temporary retreat in a space surrounded by nature and a lively artistic community. Those interested may choose any of the possibilities offered on our list. Housing can be booked for a period of min. 2 weeks and max. 2 months. This initiative is designed to bring together resources, spaces, and knowledge. It facilitates the meeting between people of different origins, backgrounds, and ideas with the common interest of being part of a temporary community based on caring, sharing experiences, and knowledge. In order to apply, check out our offers in the list (https://aadk.es/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/AADKSpain_Crossing_V3.pdf), then fill in the form.

title: Artist Residency Opportunities at Mission Street Arts Jemez Springs, NM
description: Mission Street Arts exists to further the artistic vision of resident artists and the community by providing studio space in a scenic and supportive environment. MSA welcomes artists working in diverse fields including stone-carving, sculpture, painting, drawing, performance, printmaking, textile arts, and writing, and encourages community involvement through workshops, studio visits, and exhibits. The Jemez Springs Valley has long been known as a spiritual and creative location; a perfect place to reconnect with nature and tap into oneself. With healing hot springs, amazing hiking trails, and tranquil national parks nearby, it is the perfect place to focus on creativity. Residencies are available between March 15th to November 15th, for 1 to 8 weeks, tailored to the artist. The residence includes a private bedroom, shared bathrooms and kitchenette in addition to studio space and access to various tools and equipment.

title: Light Windows
description: Join artists and institutions around the world in illuminating artwork through windows. The HoloCenter invites you to participate in LIGHT WINDOWS, a world-wide exhibition in response to COVID-19 in conjunction with the International Day of Light. Create an installation with light in your windows or connect with a local venue to show your work. Turn windows into screens, experiment with light or illuminate artwork that is visible from outside during May 2020. Share inspiration and hope with your neighbors. Add your project to the LIGHT WINDOWS interactive map, which also enables video to share your practice, add a soundtrack or document your artwork.

title: Art Pitch Artist Residency
description: The Art Pitch residency programme is ideal for an arts practitioner who wants to take time out from their busy life and environment for a short period of quiet reflection and research. Residencies are supported but self-directed. Artists can be as solitary as they wish, although dialogue with other artists can be a valuable part of time spent at the studio and may lead to future collaborative outcomes. Works made during the residency can be exhibited in the project space by arrangement. It is well suited to anyone who enjoys spending time in nature. The Cotswolds landscape is beautiful and filled with ancient standing stones and sites of historic interest. The studio is in the Evenlode Valley and yet is within easy reach of Oxford - fifteen minutes away by train and just over an hour by train to London. Artists can stay on a small campsite beside the studio in a tent that is provided with all facilities. Wooden pods are available and plenty of Airbnb in the local area if preferred.

title: Copy of 2020 Open Call from Japanese Artist In Residence “SAIKONEON” nearby Mt.Fuji with opportunity to exhibit in Tokyo
description: Saiko Neon is an artist-in-residence set up on the shore of Lake Saiko, one of Fuji Five Lakes in Yamanashi Prefecture. Lake Saiko is located in the foot of Fuji, less than two hours away from Tokyo, and offers a glimpse of the magnificent natural environment and various Japanese cultures. The facility is a former campsite that has been refurbished and approximately 300 square meters. The entire site is approximately 6000 square meters including the back mountain, and has a total of three private spaces for artists. You can concentrate on research and production activities in the studios and common spaces, which have been remodeled in a modern way while taking advantage of the characteristics of Japanese houses such as tatami. Located between the lake and the large back mountain, our facility is also suitable for indoor activities as well as outdoor activities and performances. In addition, we have partnerships with the gallery space near Nakameguro and Daikanyama areas, one of Tokyo'

title: Open Call : suclpture and installation artist residency and festival "Sculpt Tale", China
description: NY20+ China wants to open the dialogue among different countries in the field of sculpture and installation art. Free, diverse and open public art. Artists are invited to create and exhibit in a space of 67000 m2 in the open air of the park in NY20 + Art Center. The residence has a duration of one month, artists can choose the month during 2020-2021 (after the coronavirus) which suits her/him for the residence, The residence offers the possibility for artists to initiate and finalize a project by benefiting from the support of the NY20 + art center, promotion for works and artists. NY20 + will pay for accommodation and 3 meals in the art center during the residency as well as expenses for creation, artworks' materials, Round-trip plane tickets to the art center will be the responsibility of the artists. Open call for the whole year 2020-2021, residency duration：around a month per artist Festival will be held in January 2021 to exhibit the artists' arworks.

title: Artists in reisdency program fresco,mural painting, street art "Rubik's Cube" China
organizationName: A L T O Art Residency
description: Rubik's Cube，mural, fresco, painting artist residency project. With more than 40 containers waiting to be extended to various physical spaces beyond imagination, this container renovation project, aims at letting the multidimensional geometry cross the gate of space, and build the bridge of different worlds, various arts and cultures. Based on NY20+ International Art Village’s large-scale art ecology and over 200 Chengdu-based artists. Under the premise that the original ecology should be retained, we will add contemporary art, street art culture and industrial culture and let artists create each or each group of containers. Artists residency duration : 1 month Accommondation, 3 meals, creation materials pay by NY20+ Plane tickets pay by artists.

title: Healing with Nature
description: Our program focuses on the research on nature, how to live healthy ecological lifestyle and how tropical herbs and spice in Malaysia could prevent disease. Participants are encourage to share their knowledge about plants, meditation and explore the possibilities on sound and visual arts with the nature. Through the dialogue with nature, health and creativities, this program aim to give peacefulness to the local community in a subtle way.

title: A promissary note in urbanism: Hejduk's drawn and built work
description: First of the two talks about entering the continuous foyer of architecture cosmos connecting urban fabric and landscapes, highwalks and underground, east and west, megastructures, cafes, socialist housing complexes and public thresholds.

title: D2P residency for Drawing Performance - March 2021
description: The D2P Residency program is a unique opportunity for new and developing professional artists and art students to engage in the dynamic artistic discipline of drawing performance art. The program provides the foundation to develop drawing and performance skills and to translate creative practice into live action. This rigorous 15 days structured program of mentored residency includes one-on-one tutorials, workshops, intensive studio time, studio visits and artist talks by UK drawing and performance artists. The program is headed by artist and curator Ram Samocha, who is internationally acclaimed and the founder of Draw to Perform. The residency will be located in the heart of Brighton, one of the most vibrant and colourful cities in Europe and a centre of creativity, vibrancy and progressive art. The program will also include guided tours to key exhibitions and art events in Brighton and London and will end with a day of live drawing performances.

title: Residency and retreat in Italy
description: La Macina di San Cresci offers a unique opportunity for artists to work in historical artist studio: the oldest church in all of Chianti, built in the 10th century, painstakingly restored by two lifelong art lovers skilled in design and architecture. At La Macina, artists can find whatever sort of process they need; we have a thriving and close-knit community made up of visiting artists, but there is plenty of peace and quiet for those who seek relaxation and escape. Residents can take classes in fresco, watercolor, painting. Artists will also have the opportunity to explore the surrounding areas on outings to local sites with cultural and historical significance. We actively promote the work of all our artists through exhibition and open studios. We publish a yearbook “The Artistic Time” and collaborate with University of Florence, Tuscany Region, Municipality of Greve in Chianti and Tuscany Film Commission to the realization of artistic projects, land art, street art.

title: Young Yan Artists Residence Program 2019
description: Young Yan Artists Residence Program encourages and supports potential young artists to find inspiration and create artworks during the 2-month residence in Yan Garden, Dongguan, with all the necessary living space, work studio and facilities provided, along with a RMB 20,000 funding.

title: 3 hour Remote Micro-Residency
description: The Holes in the Wall Collective Remote Residency: A three-hour micro-residency in your own space. While many of us are doing everything from home, finding time and space can be more and more challenging. Whether you are writing a novel...building anti-racist curriculum...editing your film...finishing an article...designing climate adaptation models...studying algorithmic bias...making a practice of self-care so you can keep giving on the ground...strategizing getting out the vote...choreographing a piece...programming health databases...or... The HWC Remote residency provides just the right amount of accountability and feedback for your process. We are especially keen on inviting multi-disciplinary artists looking at research, policy, design, ecology or other complex issues and challenges. Free to apply and participate.

title: RESIDENCIA COLOMBIA UPCOMING
description: The residency promotes the artistic development providing a space to stay and create. Indulge in a creative retreat, far from the city with everything you need to nourish creativity, write, concentrate, focus, visualise and develop ideas, within a tropical environment.We concentrate on individuality and contribute in the comfort of the space to encourage creative introspection. The residency is located in the town of Ricaurte 3:30 hours away from the town of Bogotá, near the Magdalena river. We have a unique confortable environment for creative independent endeavour far from common distractions, ideal to concentrate on your personal development. The residency includes the stay in one apartment in a private condominium that has two pools, jacuzzis, gym, paths for exercising or jogging. It can be occupied by one or two artists. There are supermarkets near by. Materials for writing or making your artworks are provided by the artist .

title: 1-ON-1 ONSITE – Draw to Perform Mentorship Program
description: The Draw to Perform mentorship program for Drawing Performance practice. What does the program offer? 1-ON-1 is a unique program that offers professional artists and art students an opportunity for personally tailored mentorship in the art of drawing performance. The program is guided and mentored by Ram Samocha, a nationally and internationally acclaimed drawing performance artist and the founder of Draw to perform. The sessions will take place mostly in the studio but would also include optimal gallery tours or other relevant artistic experiences, and are subject to any restriction dictated by the pandemic. The mentorship program is in Lewes, the beautiful county town of East Sussex, which is a town with ancient roots well known for its artistic creativity and a long-standing orientation towards art and craft. The guest artist will need to suggest in the application the suitable dates for this one-week program.

title: 1-ON-1 ONLINE – Draw to Perform Online Mentorship Program
description: 1-ON-1 ONLINE is a unique program that offers professional artists and art students an opportunity for personally tailored mentorship in the art of drawing performance. The program is guided and mentored by Ram Samocha, a nationally and internationally acclaimed drawing performance artist and the founder of Draw to perform. What is Drawing Performance? Drawing performance is a multidisciplinary form of art, which focuses on the use of drawing as a performative tool, and on sharing the creative process with the audience via live action. Using a wide range of methods of artistic expression (i.e. mark making, dance, light & sound) the artists creates a dialogue with the viewer while exploring how drawing can be used as a way to communicate and to collaborate. How is the program constructed? This mentorship is a weeklong online program, designed for a single artist. It includes daily Skype/Zoom sessions, creative exercises, artistic brainstorming and personalized coaching.

title: FREE MENTORSHIP PROGRAM– OPEN CALL
description: Image Threads is excited to offer a free online mentorship program. For this initiative, the collective members as well as other participating photographers and bookmakers will be making themselves available to those looking for periodic dialogue and critique on an ongoing body of photographic work intended for book form. Mentoring is free of charge and will take place virtually on a bi-weekly basis, over the course of 2-3 months (a more precise schedule will be determined by each mentor and participant.) As the program is being conducted on a volunteer basis, each mentor will be selecting a limited number of projects—those we feel are best-suited to the format and to our mentors’ respective areas of expertise. In the spirit of Image Threads’ mission, preference will be given to individuals without access to comparable educational opportunities. For an up to date list of currently available mentors, please visit imagethreads.org

title: Fall Call at "Palazzo del Gatto", in the hearth of Italy
description: Our residency program provides creative artists across disciplines, with both emerging and established careers, with the opportunity to create work in a new context, to establish professional contacts and standards and to engage with the community. During their residency, artists are asked to develop a project that establishes a relationship with the territory and/or its inhabitants. Artists have opportunities to interact with locals and to visit the surroundings. At the end of the residency works are exhibited to the community. Please visit our website for all information: http://www.palazzodelgatto.it

title: Vancouver Island Artist Residency - Ongoing Applications
organizationName: The Ou Gallery on Vancouver Island
description: The Ou-telier is a personable and process based experience; a quiet place to decompress, experiment, research, play, and make space to develop new ideas. The building was a boatbuilding workshop, so you can feel the history in the old fir floors and layers of resin. Fall asleep to the sound of the creek going by, and wake up to the green of Maple trees and ivy overlooking the water. When taking breaks from the studio, spend time in the patio garden or walk ‘The Great Trail’ nearby. We are deeply grateful to call the Cowichan Valley home, and respectfully acknowledge that these lands are part of the traditional Coast Salish territory of the Quw’utsun and the Hul’qumin’num Treaty Group including T'Sou-Ke, Malahat, Halalt, S'tzuminus, Penelakut, Lyackson, Co We hope to share our journey with you by making an inclusive community space where together we can create and experience the wonderful world of art.

title: Open Call for Artists: ongoing deadline
description: Studio 88 Artist Residency is a space to play, share, learn, make mistakes and experiment in the northern Thai town of Doi Saket. Set in a rural landscape just 30 minutes from the cultural city of Chiangmai, Studio 88 gives time and space to focus on creating. The aim of the residency is to provide time out from the busy day-to-day life in order to spend time in a tranquil space to create and think. There is no pressure to produce anything by the end of the residency, although the team can help to facilitate connections with galleries or other initiatives if the resident is interested. In the first week Sasiwimon Wongjarin (Aom), an international arts manager and a native of Doi Saket, will introduce the residents to the space and the local context through a series of studio tours and site visits. Additionally, where possible she can provide any additional information about local artist initiatives relevant to each artist’s interests. The residency is an open format.

title: Now Accepting Writers-in-Residence for 2019!
description: Rockvale Writers' Colony is nestled in the rolling hills of Middle Tennessee, just 40 miles south of the bustling hub of Nashville. Writers can stay from 1 - 4 weeks in their own private bedroom, complete with ensuite bathroom. Plenty of common areas are available for independent work and several more private structures are available for those who desire complete solitude to finish their writing project. Writers in the Main Farmhouse are welcome to share the large, fully-equipped kitchen, but must bring their own food to prepare. RWC exists to support, promote, and educate writers of all backgrounds who write in any genre. We aim to provide a safe, comfortable, and inspiring environment where writers can settle in as “writers in residence” to work on a writing project.

title: INSTINC Residency Programme (Singapore)
description: Established in 2004, INSTINC is an artist-run institution that promotes a new language of art to realize a wide array of art forms, including but not limited to installation, performance and video art. In 2009, INSTINC launched its own Artist-in-Residency programme to provide a unique framework for young artists with limited experience to bypass large-scale institutional residences and take on a space where they are able to engage in various experiments and cultivate professional and personal connections. Our artist residents are welcomed to our building's facilities, including the gym, pool, and jacuzzi. In addition, we also commit to assisting our artists with media campaign and exhibition setup, using our existing connections to the Singaporean art world. Artists can choose to stay between 1 and 3 months at a reasonable rate. If you are interested in learning more about INSTINC and the programme, please email ENQUIRIES@INSTINC.COM or check out our website WWW.INSTINC.COM

title: SHORT-TERM CERAMICS ARTIST IN RESIDENCE PROGRAM
organizationName: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
description: The purpose of the Artist in Residence Program is to offer artists the opportunity to use the studio space at Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design. Residents must be self-directed, able to work independently, able to conduct themselves in a professional manner and to work cooperatively within a shared studio. The Centre offers residencies to artists in ceramics. Artists in residence are given access to these studios at a subsidized studio rental rate.

title: A.I.R. NYC: Live-Work Space in Brooklyn Artists' Community
description: · Every 2nd Tuesday of the month, we invite fellow artists and other creatives/cultural workers for a salon-style gathering where you can present your work to a very receptive audience of local artist peers and other arts professionals and appreciators · We host monthly artists' dinners for our international and NYC-based creative colleagues · During the warm months, we use the roof deck as a stage for creative productions across several disciplines · You can organize open studio events during your stay (we’ll help you!) · Various collaborative productions can potentially also be hosted at our satellite platform, Last Frontier NYC A community of hardworking artists, Mothership NYC has no outside funding, so everybody onboard must cover their own rent. But knowing full well the brutal reality of the NYC real-estate market, we wish to make a sojourn with us feasible also for peers of limited means and offer 1 free month-long stay annually: www.noosphere-arts.nyc/residency-award/

title: RESIDENCY CALL | Self-Directed Artist in Residence (Vernon, BC) | Call for Applications | Ongoing
description: CURRENT + UPCOMING AVAILABILITY: Fogliano Room: 2020: immediately - April 4th. June 8th - October 31st. December 1st onwards. Caetani Room: 2020: March 11th onwards. Sermoneta Room: 2020: Apr. 8th - 29th. Nov. 1st onwards. DATES: ongoing availability (minimum 2 weeks, maximum 3 months) RATES: between $10-$30/night depending on room + season APPLICATION DEADLINE: anytime NOTIFICATION DEADLINE: within 5 days of application being submitted WHO IS ELIGIBLE: Open to emerging and established artists and creatives (of all disciplines) INCLUDED IN THE RESIDENCY: for a reasonable fee (between $10-$30/night depending on room + season) artists stay in their own room with shared accommodations (kitchen, bathroom, living room, entryway) at the Caetani Cultural Centre (a heritage house walking distance of downtown Vernon.) If desired, artists booked for 4+ weeks are offered the opportunity to teach a workshop and/or host a reading/pop-up art exhibit.

title: International Conference "Theatre Between Tradition and Contemporaneity"
description: International Conference "Theatre Between Tradition and Contemporaneity" Theatre - Dance - Music - Visual & Multimedia Art - Arts Administration - Performing Arts Training - Theatre Design & Technology December 17 - 21, 2018 Retzhof Castle - Austria "Theatre Between Tradition and Contemporaneity" is the annual international multidisciplinary conference researching the Bridge between Tradition and Contemporaneity in performing arts. description: The concept of Deep Listening, as coined by Pauline Oliveros when her nascent Deep Listening Band descended into an underground cistern to perform using the space's 45-second reverb, has become increasingly vital in modern music. She described Deep Listening as "listening in every possible way to everything possible to hear no matter what one is doing". title: Where Do We Draw The Line? A drawing workshop by Adeline Kueh
description: This two-part experimental workshop will examine the poetics of Line and Stitch and the ways in which drawing may be used in our everyday practices. We will explore the relationship between drawing and the architecture of the everyday: from the ways a line may be employed as a divider that separates the self from (an)other; to drawing as a form of embodied meaning-making and storytelling across time and space. Reflecting on the inner geography of the pandemic, unpacking placeness and memory through observation of texture and surface, tracing, mark making, frottage, collage, decollage, we will look at the ways the line can become a form of stitching or mending and other kinds of meaning making. We will also examine ways of recording and translating our body, our pulse, breath, blood pressure, gestures and movements in our surroundings as a kind of translation project.

title: THE EARTH OF (3): Ruptures and Reckonings
description: The Earth Of: Ruptures and Reckonings is a collective virtual space of inquiry. Through writing and discourse we investigate how to manifest and inhabit the fractures that pervade our lives, allowing for the creative space to grow organically through digressions, tangents, musings, and synchronistic linkages. What does it mean when humanity crosses a threshold of such significance it manifests as a rupture, when the world is on the cusp? The brain wants to organize, filter, and separate out. Yet, beyond the confusion perpetrated by language that fails to adequately define, are spaces. We find meaning when we implicitly inhabit these spaces—gestures that guide the cracks to spread toward shattering. These moments of rupture burst forth from gesture into reckoning, exposing us to what is real and true and essential.

title: SONIC TRAILS Theatres of Archimagination
description: What is the pulse of a city when citizens go silent? What are the scenes of a city when society recedes? What qualities and processes remain when everyday activities are abandoned? As the city enters a state of “Lockdown,” the urban environment loses its most distinctive element: human presence. Nonetheless, it would be a mistake to consider the city abandoned. As human activity withdraws, other processes and activities come into focus. Cars pass through empty streets, trees sway in deserted parks, birds roam uninhabited spaces. In Sonic Trails: Lockdown, visitors are immersed in various events of a lockdown city occurring regardless of their presence. Using multiple audio-visual samples of these urban phenomena, the installation creates a new inhabitable place using layered projections and four loudspeakers. Artificial intelligence algorithms determine the composition of this environment in a constant process of deconstruction and reconfiguration.

title: Grappling with and engaging the cultural implications of homelessness
description: In the brutal winter of 2013, curator Rhoda Rosen and artist Billy McGuiness, living at opposite ends of the 26-mile-long north-south Red Line of Chicago’s metro service, launched a practice of preparing home cooked meals every Saturday night and going out to the blustery platforms at one end of the line or the other to share them (with proper tablecloths, plates and silverware) with some of the people experiencing homelessness who had taken to living out their nights on the metro trains and were being forced to disembark between rides. From that initial action grew a widening community and the insight that on top of being houseless, people experiencing homelessness were living out a sort of exile from the city’s vital cultural life. The community themselves set out to remedy that situation, systematically challenging Chicago’s cultural institutions to make room and provision for them.

title: SIX SHORT FILMS BY BILL MORRISON
description: “One of the most adventurous American filmmakers” —Variety Bill Morrison makes films that reframe long-forgotten moving images. His work has premiered at the New York, Sundance, Telluride and Venice film festivals. Morrison had a mid-career retrospective at MoMA in 2014. His found footage opus Decasia (2002) was the first film of the 21 st century to be selected to the Library of Congress’ National Film Registry. The Great Flood (2013) was recognized with the Smithsonian Ingenuity Award for historical scholarship. Dawson City: Frozen Time (2016) was listed as one of the best films of the decade (2010s) by the Associated Press, Los Angeles Times, Vanity Fair and others. In 2021 Morrison became a member of the documentary branch of the Academy of Motion Pictures Arts and Sciences. His most recent feature-length doc, The Village Detective: a song cycle (2021) is being released theatrically by Kino Lorber in September 2021.

title: An Architectonic Technological Sublimity
description: In the last few decades, US Space Agency NASA has constructed an astonishingly vast, kinetic, architectonic structure, one spanning the entire Solar System. This ever-evolving edifice comprises recognizably architectural forms: the buildings of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California; NASA HQ in Washington and various mission control centers; a global network of giant dish antennae; and rocket assembly, testing and launching facilities. But these would be meaningless without another principal component: the intricate spacecraft it has sent vaulting to all the major worlds of our planetary system, and the football-field sized International Space Station. Some of these extraordinarily advanced interplanetary robots are no bigger than a grand piano, and the largest is a bit smaller than a city bus. A cat’s-cradle webwork of signals connects them to Earth, its chains of zeroes and ones slinging across the void and returning images and data.
